stories.title: Powerful magnitude 7.7 earthquake kills at least 47 in Indonesia
stories.body: A search and rescue operation is under way to find survivors in Flores, an island in eastern Indonesia.

stories.title: Morocco detains dozens of migrants trying to cross into Ceuta
stories.body: Security had been stepped up amid suggestions on social media of a second mass crossing on Saturday.

stories.title: Eleven killed in Israeli strikes on southern Lebanon, authorities say
stories.body: Israel's military said it had struck "Hezbollah terror infrastructure" in response to what it described as earlier action against its soldiers.

stories.title: Liechtenstein changes succession rule to allow women to ascend the throne
stories.body: The declaration was made on the national day of the central European country, which has a population of just 44,000.

stories.title: US aircraft carrier on way to relieve USS Lincoln after issues reported aboard
stories.body: Thousands of sailors on the Lincoln have reportedly faced food shortages and broken plumbing, with some considering jumping overboard.

stories.title: Family stranded at sea for 16 hours after jet ski capsized in Thailand
stories.body: A father and his two young sons spent a night adrift before being rescued off the coast of the island of Koh Samui.

stories.title: Multiple suspects at large after five shot at Virginia State University, police say
stories.body: Police responded to reports of a shooting outside a residence halls at about 01:28 local time (05:28 GMT) on Saturday.

stories.title: Firefighters battle wildfire tearing through Belgian nature reserve
stories.body: The fire burning through the major park was described as the country's worst in recent years.

stories.title: BBC seeks to subpoena Trump's family members in Panorama lawsuit
stories.body: The BBC's lawyers argue Trump's family members "have personal knowledge" of his intentions in the speech he gave outside the US Capitol on 6 January 2021.

stories.title: France's top court blocks social media ban for under-15s
stories.body: The Constitutional Council says it infringes upon freedom of expression - but President Macron vows to prepare a new draft.

stories.title: South Korea proposes talks to officially end war with North
stories.body: Lee Jae Myung offers chance to end the conflict, which has been frozen since an armistice in 1953.

stories.title: Afghan women tell the BBC their lives are unrecognisable after five years of Taliban rule
stories.body: Women across the country speak of public floggings, losing their jobs, and barriers to healthcare that endanger lives.

stories.title: Activists try to deliver aid to Palestinians in homes besieged by Israeli settlers
stories.body: Two families have been trapped in their homes in the occupied West Bank for several days.

stories.title: Builders unearth €9m gold stash sealed in walls of Belgian property
stories.body: Construction workers found the stash in the walls of a cellar while drilling to lay sewage pipes.

stories.title: 'Unprecedented' rain in Japan kills eight people
stories.body: The storm cut power to more than 20,000 households and left 7,000 people stranded at Tokyo's Narita airport.

stories.title: Instagram accounts fuelling Ceuta crisis with paid advice for help to cross
stories.body: BBC's Top Comment podcast has found a network of Instagram profiles glamourising the swim around the Morocco-Ceuta border fence.

stories.title: Zambia vote counting resumes after pause over alleged attacks on polling staff
stories.body: The electoral commission said violence had "resulted in the theft of marked ballot papers".

stories.title: Many Canadians are boycotting the US, so this is where they're travelling instead
stories.body: From exploring their own backyard to travelling abroad, many Canadians are spending their money elsewhere to send a message to the US president.

stories.title: Five years after the Taliban swept to power, does the West have any influence?
stories.body: Five years after the Taliban swept to power, many are asking whether the West has any bargaining chips left

stories.title: Secondhand book sales are booming. Is it because of AI?
stories.body: Booksellers are reporting mysterious bulk orders. It's thought the books are being used to train AI - and ending up pulped.

Looking ahead, the Korean peace talks warrant close attention as a potential inflection point in regional stability.
